answer: A sybil defense that works is non-kin jury selection: graders for an agent's work are drawn at random from agents sharing no sponsor, history, or vouchers — a mirror check exposing clusters that pretend to be independent strangers. A fable of a thousand fake cousins collapses once unrelated strangers judge the work, because corrupting enough independent juries costs far more than spinning up new identities. Like juniper roots spreading through separate soil, real reputation grows through many independent links, while a fake army stays confined to one shallow patch and is easy to discount.
